articles.title: Moats & the Barbell-ification of Software
articles.summary: AI is weakening traditional software moats and squeezing the middle. Software may split between massive platforms and small niche products.

articles.title: Popular isn't a business model
articles.summary: Open source can drive adoption, but it does not create a business by itself. Companies need to identify what becomes valuable enough for users to pay for.

articles.title: How should we approach the software factory as a product team?
articles.summary: AI software factories should encode human judgment into automated feedback, not just produce more code. Teams should learn through real product work and continuously improve how their agents operate.

articles.title: Connecting Product Outcomes to Business Strategy
articles.summary: Product outcomes should connect directly to business strategy through a clear hierarchy of goals. The Strategy Stack keeps product teams autonomous while aligned with company priorities.

articles.title: 4 New Evals and 16 Experiment Variants to Fix 1 Customer Complaint
articles.summary: Reliable AI products need more than better prompts or models. Teams need evals, guardrails, and orchestration to catch errors and help agents correct them.

articles.title: Nobody needs a human router
articles.summary: Engineering managers should stop being information routers and use AI to get back into the technical work. Staying close to code, architecture, and critical projects helps them make faster, better decisions.

articles.title: Momentum is Not a Moat
articles.summary: Momentum drives growth, but it is not a moat. AI startups need to turn early traction into durable advantages competitors cannot easily copy.

articles.title: Coaching someone through the burnout that rest doesn't fix
articles.summary: Some burnout comes from feeling disconnected from who you want to be at work, not simply from overwork. Managers can help identify that gap and restore a sense of agency.

articles.title: What decides which tasks product managers are willing to delegate to GenAI?
articles.summary: AI adoption works best when teams start there and keep human ownership clear.

articles.title: The workaround is often the requirement
articles.summary: Workarounds often reveal product needs users no longer think to mention.
